function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
The user wants the temperature forecast for New York City next week. We need to use the Open-Meteo API. The user didn't specify coordinates, but we can use NYC coordinates: latitude 40.7128, longitude -74.0060. We need to get the forecast for the next week. The Open-Meteo API supports daily forecasts. We can request daily temperature_2m_max and min. We'll call the function.

We need to provide the function call with the correct parameters. The function signature expects:

- url: string
- headers optional
- timeout optional
- params: dictionary with latitude, longitude, elevation optional
- allow_redirects optional
- auth optional
- cert optional
- cookies optional
- proxies optional
- stream optional
- verify optional

We need to set the URL to the Open-Meteo API endpoint. According to documentation, the endpoint is "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". We need to pass query parameters: latitude=40.7128, longitude=-74.0060, daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min, timezone=America/New_York. Also we might want to specify start_date and end_date. For next week, we need to compute dates. But we can just let the API return the next 7 days. The API returns daily data for the next 7 days by default? Actually, the API returns daily data for the next 7 days if not specified. But we can specify start_date and end_date. Let's compute start_date as tomorrow's date. Today is 2026-07-20. Next week would be 2026-07-21 to 2026-07-27 inclusive. So start_date=2026-07-21, end_date=2026-07-27. We'll pass those as query parameters.

Thus the function call will be:

{
  "url": "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast",
  "params": {
    "latitude": 40.7128,
    "longitude": -74.0060,
    "daily": "temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min",
    "timezone": "America/New_York",
    "start_date": "2026-07-21",
    "end_date": "2026-07-27"
  }
}

We don't need to set other optional fields. That should work.

We'll then parse the result and give the user the forecast.
